current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 19:1 opens with the distinct qinah-command onset וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.1) ('and you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel') -- not a word-event formula and not a son-of-man address, but the genre-naming command proper to a lament. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own colophon, MT 19:14, the whole verse וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֨יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.19.14), whose last clause names its own genre a second time ('this is a lamentation, and it is used as a lamentation'), matched by a pe recorded on this same verse. A pe also falls mid-chapter, on 19:9, at the close of the lion-cubs figure -- לְמַ֗עַן לֹא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.9) ('so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel') -- immediately before the second figure opens at 19:10, אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.19.10) ('your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water'). That internal mark is disclosed and weighed, not adopted as a row seam: the colophon at 19:14 names the whole composition, both figures together, a single lamentation, so the span is kept as one row rather than split at its own internal parashah break.
